topic: Unveiling Conic Sections: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres
target_audience: High school students interested in geometry or introductory college math students.

outline.topic: Unveiling Conic Sections: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in geometry or introductory college math students.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Conic Anatomy
sections.content: Define a double cone (nappe) and a plane. Explain that a conic section is the intersection of these two. Introduce the goal: Why does a specific angle of a plane create a circle, ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola?
sections.example: Visualize a flashlight beam: A cone of light hitting a flat wall creates different shapes as you tilt the flashlight.

sections.title: Introduction to Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Introduce the 'Dandelin Spheres'—spheres tucked inside the cone, tangent to both the cone and the slicing plane. State the core insight: The points of tangency reveal the hidden geometric properties of the section.
sections.example: Imagine a tennis ball perfectly wedged inside a party hat, touching the sides and the lid simultaneously.

sections.title: The Proof Logic (Focus on Ellipse)
sections.content: Explain that the distance from any point on the conic section to the points of tangency (foci) is constant. Use the property that tangents from a point to a sphere are equal in length.
sections.example: A trail of ants walking on the ellipse; their distance to the two Dandelin points remains fixed, illustrating the 'sum of distances' definition of an ellipse.

sections.title: Visualizing the Family of Curves
sections.content: Show the animation transition: As the plane's tilt increases, the Dandelin spheres shift. When the plane is parallel to the cone's edge, one sphere 'escapes' to infinity, transitioning from an ellipse to a parabola.
sections.example: A robotic arm tilting a slicing blade through a giant block of cheese; observe how the shape changes from an oval (ellipse) to a 'U' shape (parabola) as the angle changes.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Reiterate that Dandelin spheres provide the elegant link between the 3D cone and 2D focal properties. Conclude with how this governs orbits and satellite technology.
sections.example: Kepler's laws: Planets move in elliptical orbits because the geometry of space-time gravity follows these exact conic paths.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Conic Anatomy
lecture_lines: Meet the cone and the slicing plane.
animations: Draw a cone outline in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the base circle in bright yellow (#FFFF00).
Label the vertex with 'V' in blue (#0000FF).
Draw a plane slicing the cone in red (#FF0000).
Highlight the resulting intersection as 'Ellipse' in green (#00FF00).

storyboard.title: Introduction to Dandelin Spheres
lecture_lines: Dandelin spheres hide inside the cone.
They touch the cone and the plane.
animations: Create a transparent cone in gray (#808080).
Place a small sphere inside the cone in light blue (#ADD8E6).
Place a second, larger sphere below it in light blue (#ADD8E6).
Position a plane tangent to both spheres in red (#FF0000).
Show the intersection points as focal points in yellow (#FFFF00).

storyboard.title: The Proof Logic (Focus on Ellipse)
lecture_lines: Tangents from point to sphere are equal.
animations: Represent the ellipse on the plane in green (#00FF00).
Draw lines from any ellipse point to two spheres.
Show line segments length consistency in orange (#FFA500).
Label focal points F1 and F2 in cyan (#00FFFF).
Animate point P moving along the ellipse path.

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Family of Curves
lecture_lines: Tilt the plane to change shapes.
The sphere shifts with the tilt.
animations: Rotate the plane angle to create a parabola in magenta (#FF00FF).
Rotate the plane angle further to create a hyperbola.
Highlight the changing Dandelin sphere positions in light blue.

storyboard.title: Summary and Real-world Application
animations: Show a summary table of conic section types.
Flash the focus-directrix property in yellow (#FFFF00).
Briefly display a telescope or architectural arch example.
